findings.claim: `reboots_sent` is incremented for every row in `attempts`, including reservations with no recorded outcome. The service durably inserts that reservation before calling `client.reboot()`, so a crash in between can leave an attempt counted as a reboot sent when no command was issued. This makes the report's documented “reboots sent” metric overstate known sends.
findings.title: The report counts reserved attempts as reboots sent

findings.claim: The report selects `durations[len(durations) // 2]` as `outage_median_s`. For an even number of measured outages this returns only the upper middle duration rather than the median (the average of the two middle values), so the documented median is inaccurate for those samples.
findings.title: Even-sized outage samples report the upper middle value, not the median

findings.claim: The new preflight-failure handling durably auth-latches on `UNSUPPORTED`. But the preflight calls `GetDeviceInformation`, while the unsupported-reboot claim concerns `SystemReboot`; a camera rejecting the read operation can therefore be blocked from recovery until operator acknowledgement even though reboot support was never tested. The fault classifier maps generic unsupported-operation faults to `UNSUPPORTED`.
findings.title: Unsupported preflight operation can latch recovery as if reboot were unsupported

findings.claim: The report increments `reboots_sent` for every row in `attempts`, but dispatch records that row during reservation before calling `client.reboot()`. A process interruption after reservation and before the send therefore appears in the report as a reboot sent, contrary to the report's documented meaning.
findings.title: Report can overstate reserved attempts as reboots sent

findings.claim: `reboots_sent` is incremented for every row in `attempts`, but attempts are durably inserted before `client.reboot()` is called. If the process stops in between, the report still counts a reboot as sent even though no ONVIF request was issued, making the effectiveness report inaccurate.
findings.title: Report counts reserved attempts as reboots sent

findings.claim: The catalogue’s `productIDs` trims surrounding whitespace before those IDs are requested from StoreKit, but the joiner looks up products using the original, untrimmed catalogue values. For an ID with surrounding whitespace, StoreKit can return the requested product while the join fails to associate it with its plan, so that cadence is absent from the subscription list.
findings.title: Normalized product IDs are joined using their unnormalized values

findings.claim: Catalogue `productIDs` trims surrounding whitespace before requesting StoreKit products, but the joiner looks up StoreKit results using the untrimmed monthly/yearly catalogue values. If a configured ID has surrounding whitespace, StoreKit can return the trimmed ID while the joiner drops that cadence, leaving the plan unavailable despite a successful product request.
findings.title: Trimmed catalogue product IDs fail to join StoreKit results

findings.claim: The admin and cart rate limits only track and reject requests when CF-Connecting-IP is present, and use its value as the tracking key. A network-level Cloudflare-only ingress restriction could mitigate this, but none is established in the reviewed configuration.

The README still advises that the data volume is the safety record (ev_069b69203dce151a). The API serves /stats, /history, and the new /report, with no authentication. Users who copy the example and run `fwatch serve` outside a container, as the example's own comment anticipates, will expose these endpoints on every host interface. The comment says to prefer 127.0.0.1 outside a container, but the default now points the other way. Mitigating factors: the compose file publishes no port by default, and the change is documented. findings.claim: In BASE, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN latched the incident durably via a 'latch_incident' store op, and the 'AUTH_FAILED' path added 'auth_latch'. In HEAD, on_outcome sends OUTCOME_UNKNOWN into BOOT_GRACE with no store op (policy.py ~1138-1140). When boot grace expires, on_tick calls _latch(), which sets only in-memory state to LATCHED and emits an event, with no StoreOp. service.py's _iterate passes the on_tick decision as _handle_events(decision.events, []), so store_ops are dropped. The durable incident therefore stays unlatched. On the next snapshot, _process_no_frames returns early only for BOOT_GRACE or RECOVERY_PENDING, or when rt.store_latched is set (refreshed from the store each snapshot, so False). With store_armed true, it sets rt.state = SUSPECT, which overwrites the in-memory LATCHED. Check 14 (incident.latched) then passes. Only the per-camera cooldown (1h runtime), daily budget (3/24h), and global spacing still apply, so a second reboot can be proposed and sent in the same outage once those clear. This violates the policy invariant 'A latched outage never receives a second attempt' and the operations doc's troubleshooting statement that after OUTCOME_UNKNOWN 'there will not be a second attempt this outage'. The durable latch is also lost on restart.
findings.title: Boot-grace expiry and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN no longer durably latch; a second reboot can follow in the same outage

findings.claim: The architecture amendment fixes retail to deployment_profile=retail with delivery_mode=public_consumer, and the lifecycle CLI enforces that mapping (PROFILES in tools/installation_lifecycle.py, plus the expected-mode check). findings.claim: be_lms_dev_nonprod_https routes to `server lms_dev_nonprod 172.31.1.60:443`. Since HAProxy forwards Host lms-dev.smartcompliancesystems.com.au with ProxyPreserveHost on the legacy side, lms-dev requests are likely to fall through to the effectivepolicy WordPress vhost, or fail, rather than reaching the lms-dev PHP-FPM pool. findings.claim: The HEAD runbook says the shield fields are observe-only (shield_action=allow, score=0) and says 'Do not enable blocking rules until config is repo-managed and deploy/rollback scripts exist.' This change adds a repo-managed scs-edge-01 HAProxy config with active deny paths: 421 for unknown hosts, 404 for never-serve paths, 403 for probe, xmlrpc, and forged-cart paths, and 429 for rate limits. Searches for HAProxy deploy or rollback tooling return only Drupal/PHP release scripts and the nfpm packaging entries, not an HAProxy-specific deploy or rollback path. The repo is therefore not yet in the state the runbook requires before blocking can be enabled. Uncertainty: the runbook may have been superseded, and the rollback tooling may live outside this repo under another name.

findings.claim: plans/m2-0-receipt.md (lines 42-47) says `deferredToM2A` registers `STORE-06 → STORE_06_twoWritersCompeteForOneSession` as required certifying evidence, and that a RED probe showed the gate failing with `satisfied=[… STORE-06 …]`. In the code, `requiredVariants` is computed only from `requiredEvidence`, and `deferredToM2A` is used only in a post-hoc loop asserting `!report.satisfied.contains(caseID)`. STORE-06 has no results row in the ingested runner output, so it is always 'missing' and the assertion is trivially true. The gate cannot fail on the mechanism the receipt describes, so the claimed RED probe cannot have exercised this code, and the STORE-06 'hard gate' is not an executable control. Any future false STORE-06 certification would only be caught if a result row for that case appeared under a matching function name. The receipt and the test need to agree on what the gate actually checks.
findings.title: Receipt says STORE-06 is a required certifying gate, but the code never registers it

findings.claim: CaseResult is a public Codable type. The diff adds `public var evidenceTier: EvidenceLayer` with CodingKey `evidence_tier`. The synthesized decoder requires that key, so any previously serialized result record without it will fail to decode. The default of `.pure` applies only to the memberwise init, not to decoding. Consumers receive `.pure` only when they construct the value in code. In-repo search found no JSON decoder for CaseResult, so the breakage is latent for external CI or `./dev coverage` consumers. The receipt does not mention this wire-format change. Fail-closed behaviour is preserved for missing tiers, but the incompatibility itself is undocumented.
findings.title: CaseResult gains a required `evidence_tier` JSON key with no decode default

findings.claim: On HEAD, GROUP_INHIBITION_THRESHOLD = 2 is documented as the 'Number of failing enabled cameras that inhibit all automatic recovery', and the module docstring calls the 'two-camera inhibition threshold' a core loop-prevention guarantee that configuration must not weaken. That no longer matches the code: policy.py's _maybe_propose no longer returns when len(failing) >= threshold, and the BASE invariant 'No action is proposed while two or more enabled cameras are failing' was removed. The threshold now only starts a multiple_failing event and selects the MULTIPLE_CAMERAS_UNHEALTHY global state, and the phased-recovery guards are what limit recovery. Maintainers or auditors reading the constants module would get a wrong picture of the safety model. This is documentation drift with no direct runtime effect; the recovery-limiting behaviour itself is the documented change in README and operations.md.
findings.title: constants.py still documents the two-camera threshold as inhibiting all recovery

findings.claim: The module docstring says the 'two-camera inhibition threshold' is one of the 'core loop prevention guarantees' that configuration must not weaken. The GROUP_INHIBITION_THRESHOLD docstring says failing cameras 'inhibit all automatic recovery' at that count. In HEAD, _maybe_propose no longer returns when len(failing) >= GROUP_INHIBITION_THRESHOLD. The threshold now only drives the multiple_failing event, the MULTIPLE_CAMERAS_UNHEALTHY global state, and the phase-halt check. Those comments now describe behaviour the code no longer has, and they are the in-code statement of the safety rationale a maintainer would rely on.
findings.title: constants.py still documents the removed two-camera hard block as a non-configurable loop-prevention guarantee

findings.claim: BASE blocked all proposals when len(failing) >= 2, and its module invariant said 'No action is proposed while two or more enabled cameras are failing.' HEAD removes that block. Counterfactual: three cameras, porch and driveway dark, garage stably healthy, all other guards passing. BASE: _maybe_propose returns at the failing-count check, so no reboot. HEAD: candidates are sorted by bad_since, the porch check passes because the only other failing peer is accounted for and the one stable peer satisfies peers_stable, so porch is proposed for reboot while driveway is still dark. The change is documented (policy docstring, operations.md 'Several cameras failing', README) and covered by tests (test_phasing_halts_when_a_reboot_did_not_restore_frames, test_no_recovery_when_no_camera_is_healthy). Mitigating factors I verified: observe mode still fails in evaluate_action (policy.py ~897, ev_44f32f9b62dd9c3b and ev_c483736e17fc9b11); a per-camera ONVIF preflight gates each send; one attempt per outage, 1h per-camera cooldown, 3/day budget, and 5-minute global spacing still apply; and a latched camera halts further phased reboots. Uncertainty: the authorising policy is the operations doc in this same PR, not an independent policy, and I could not check whether a switch or network-wide failure with a single stable peer is handled. Treat this as a qualified advisory on a deliberate boundary change, not a confirmed defect.
findings.title: Recovery is now permitted while two or more cameras are failing, relaxing a documented safety invariant

findings.claim: The gateway authenticates its caller with env.ARCHIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN and forwards that value as the x-archive-internal-token header. The archive Worker, however, validates the header against env.ARCHIVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN, and any mismatch returns 404 (not 401). Within the repository, ARCHIVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN appears only in worker.js, and the archive Wrangler template declares no such var or secret. The gateway template declares no ARCHIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN either. So the hop works only if an out-of-band provisioning step sets the archive Worker's ARCHIVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN to the gateway's ARCHIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN value. The gateway's own unit test checks only its own forwarding, not the archive side. The M0.5-D ledger entry records a first host invocation that returned HTTP 404 with unknown origin. A name or value mismatch on this hop would produce exactly that status, so it is a plausible contributor. Uncertainty: I did not find the operator procedure that provisions these secrets, and I did not verify the deployed values. The defect is in the code contract as written, not an observed regression against BASE, which has no such files.
findings.title: Archive gateway and Worker use different secret names for the same internal token; the Worker fails closed with 404

findings.claim: README.md says the current regression suite 'passes 48 tests and 32 subtests'. This is a documentation accuracy issue with low impact; it does not change any qualification claim, and the README's 'local tests do not qualify real SCORM playback' caveat is accurate.
findings.title: README states a stale regression-suite count that the ledger in the same PR supersedes

findings.claim: HEAD routes host lms-dev.smartcompliancesystems.com.au via be_lms_dev_nonprod_https to `server lms_dev_nonprod 172.31.1.60:443 ... sni str(lms-dev...)`. The new lms-dev vhost in the same change is `<VirtualHost 172.31.1.60:9443>` with ServerName lms-dev.smartcompliancesystems.com.au and DocumentRoot /var/www/smart-lms/public. The sibling backends for portal-staging, valet-staging and UAT all target 172.31.1.60:9443 and the epcore-event instance, and the HAProxy comment says the isolated event-MPM service is the one that runs on 9443. So lms-dev requests appear to go to the :443 listener, which the runbook describes as the nonprod WordPress/epcore Apache, not to the event-MPM vhost that serves smart-lms. If :443 has no lms-dev vhost, lms-dev traffic would hit a different application or fall through to the default vhost. Uncertainty: the :443 vhost configuration is not in this change set, so the routing may be intentional. I could not confirm which vhost serves that SNI on :443.
